question: Does fixed-crop text-row alignment distinguish consecutive LP2 pages from other same-layout pairs?
scope: LP2-40–48, one continuous text-heavy run with the same border layout; all 8 adjacent pairs and all 28 nonadjacent within-run controls. Scope chosen as a coherent visual baseline, not specified by the original proposal.
crop_reason: A single central text column excludes plant margins, red side marker, top whitespace and lower page blank on all nine 2400×3600 images. No per-page crop fitting.
registration: Keep source image coordinates. Compare identical y rows, no fitted translation, scaling, rotation or elastic warp.
score: For each y row, mark occupied when more than 12 sampled pixels in the crop are grayscale below 90. Compare two masks by intersection divided by union (Jaccard).
decision: Report every pair and group descriptives. A distinctive adjacency pattern would require adjacent scores reliably above nonadjacent controls. The test cannot decide glyph or word continuation, or validate a decryption.
limits: The report did not fix target pages, cropping, transformation or success threshold.
The fixed row mask ignores rune identity and x-position.
Red enlarged initials and atypical spacing change row bands.
Pairs share pages and are not independent samples; no p-value is assigned.
